relevance_note: Single case report of a woman with a diagnosis of Blau syndrome ('A 37 year old lady with Blau syndrome'), so she is in scope by diagnosis, although no NOD2 variant or genetic test is reported for her.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a small Python script assembled the JSON and checked spans. One in-scope person, labelled 'patient' (rule 5). No NOD2/CARD15 variant is printed or tied to her: the Discussion mentions CARD15 only in general terms and her diagnosis is clinical ('the clinical picture was consistent with Blau's Syndrome'), so the variants table is empty and n_patients_reported is null. Her older sister, who 'died as a neonate shortly after birth from complex congenital heart disease', was not given a row: she was not tested and is not described as affected by Blau syndrome; this is a judgement call under the relative-scope rule. The authors' statement 'We believe that this is some form autoimmune aortitis, but further evidence is needed' is hedged, so the vasculitis/aortitis checklist item is left not reported. The finger contractures and camptodactyly were not taken as arthritis; arthritis/uveitis and other checklist items are not mentioned for her. The post-operative 1 cm pericardial fluid collection is recorded as a feature but not as pericarditis. The TOE 'suggestion of either a thrombus within the sinuses or an intramural haematoma' is hedged and was not used; mural thrombus is recorded from the operative finding. The rash is described as erythematous with no biopsy; it supports only the 'skin rash' part of the checklist item. Age 37 years is the age at referral/presentation in this report; follow-up was eight weeks after surgery. No contradictions found.

treatment_summary.value: Replacement of the aortic valve and root with a 23 mm Carbo-Seal composite mechanical prosthesis (modified Bentall's technique) with excision of the aortic sinuses, saccular aneurysm wall and laminated thrombus and reimplantation of coronary buttons; emergency re-sternotomy and evacuation of blood clots for post-operative pericardial collection; previously operated hammer toes
span: the repair was performed with replacement of the aortic valve and root using a composite graft employing a modified Bentall's technique
The aortic sinuses were excised along with most of the saccular aneurysm wall and the laminated thrombus. A 23 mm Carbo-Seal composite mechanical prosthesis was selected.
Left and right coronary buttons were anastmosed to the composite graft.
Following re-sternotomy and evacuation of blood clots
Previously operated upon hammer toes and forefoot deformity.
